chunks: Ali ibn Ja'far narrated from his brother Musa (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about the Takbir (saying Allahu Akbar) during the days of Tashriq: is it obligatory or not? He said, 'It is recommended, and if he forgets, there is no penalty upon him.' I asked him about the women: is the Takbir upon them during the days of Tashriq? He said, 'Yes, and they should not be loud.'

key_terms.وَلَا يَجْهَرْنَ: And they do not be loud/raise their voices

ai.seo_question: Is the Takbir during the days of Tashriq obligatory or recommended for men and women?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS), the distinction between obligatory and recommended acts is clarified, emphasizing that forgetting the Takbir incurs no penalty, which reflects the Shia principle of ease in ritual worship. The specific instruction for women to recite quietly highlights the general jurisprudential norm of modesty in public worship, distinguishing their practice from the louder recitation often associated with men in congregational settings. This ruling is situated within the broader context of Hajj rituals, where the days of Tashriq serve as a period of continued glorification after the main rites at Mina.
